chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The one who is fair with the people from himself, would be pleased with judging for others.
ai.seo_question: What quality makes a person suitable to judge others according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith from al-Kafi establishes that internal self-accountability (muhasabah) is the foundational criterion for external judicial authority, linking moral integrity directly to legal competence. It implies that a judge who can fairly adjudicate their own desires and flaws is best equipped to deliver impartial verdicts, a concept central to the Shia emphasis on the moral qualifications of the qadi.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from one of his companions, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The one who is fair with the people from himself, would be pleased with judging for others’.
en.sarwar: 12. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn Mahbub from certain individuals of his people from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “
Whoever yields to justice for people against his own soul is accepted to judge others’ cases.”
